title: Turn-by-Turn Route in a Tree
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree whose n nodes hold the values 1 to n, each exactly once, plus two different values start and dest that are both in the tree.

Return the directions for the shortest walk from the node holding start to the node holding dest, as a string of moves:

  • 'U' goes up to the parent,
  • 'L' goes down to the left child,
  • 'R' goes down to the right child.

The shortest walk in a tree is unique, so there is exactly one correct string. Trees are written in level order with null for a missing child.

examples.why: Up from 3 to 1, up to 5, right to 2, left to 6.
The walk turns at 2, not at the root. Going all the way up to 5 and back would not be the shortest walk.
If start is an ancestor of dest, the route has no U moves at all.

constraints: Node values are 1 … n, all distinct
start ≠ dest, both in the tree
The tree is at most 1000 levels deep
hints: The shortest walk goes up from start to some turning node, then down to dest. Which node is the turning point?
It is their lowest common ancestor. Everything from start up to it is a run of U moves; from it down to dest is a run of L and R moves.
Record the L/R path from the root to start and from the root to dest. Drop their shared prefix; the rest of start's path becomes U's, and the rest of dest's path is used as is.

explain.intuition:
In a tree there is only one simple path between two nodes, and it bends at their lowest common ancestor. Above that node the two root paths are identical, below it they split.

So write down the root-to-node directions for both, like two URL paths /R/L/L and /R/R. Cut off the common prefix, which is the route down to the turning node. The leftover part of start's path must be undone, one U per step, and the leftover part of dest's path is walked forward. It is exactly how a relative path like ../../b/c is computed between two folders.
steps: Find the root-to-node path of start as a string of L/R moves, and the same for dest. Walking up from each node with a parent map avoids deep recursion.
Count the length k of their longest common prefix.
Return 'U' repeated (startPath.length − k) times, followed by destPath from index k on.
pitfalls: Routing through the root every time. When both nodes sit in the same subtree that walk is longer than the shortest one.
Reversing the moves of start's leftover path instead of replacing them all with U. Going up never needs to know if you came from the left or the right.
Building path strings by repeated concatenation in a deep recursion. Collect moves in an array and join once.

solutions.title: Breadth-first search over the tree as a graph
solutions.idea: Treat parent and child links as edges labelled U, L, R and BFS from start until dest is reached, then rebuild the moves.

solutions.title: Root paths minus their common prefix
solutions.idea: Get the L/R path from the root to each node, strip the shared prefix (the way down to the common ancestor), and turn start's leftover into U moves.

followups: Answer many (start, dest) queries on the same tree quickly. What would you precompute?
The tree is a general tree where each node has any number of children, labelled by index. What changes?
